title: The Biggest Chip Stocks All Yield Under 1%. Here's Where the Cash Actually Goes.
author: Daniel Sparks
description: Major chip stocks (Nvidia, Broadcom, Taiwan Semiconductor, and Applied Materials) all offer dividend yields below 1% despite strong profitability. Instead of dividends, these companies return cash to shareholders through stock buybacks and capital investments in manufacturing capacity and equipment, with each company prioritizing different uses for their cash flows.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recently increased dividend 25-fold and returned $20 billion to shareholders in latest quarter through buybacks, with $80 billion additional repurchase authorization approved. Strong shareholder return commitment despite low yield.

Paid largest actual dividend checks ($3.1 billion) among the group with minimal capital expenditure ($231 million), demonstrating efficient capital allocation and strong cash generation relative to investment needs.

Prioritizes capital investment in manufacturing capacity (raised 2026 budget to $60-64 billion) over dividends, which is necessary for maintaining competitive edge but limits current shareholder income. Dividend growth is secondary to fab expansion.

Distributed nearly all operating cash ($845 million) through combination of buybacks and dividends, with 15% dividend increase marking ninth consecutive annual increase, demonstrating consistent shareholder-friendly capital allocation.

title: Semiconductor Equipment Makers vs. Chip Designers: Who's Actually Winning the AI Cycle?
author: Chris Neiger
description: The article compares semiconductor equipment makers (ASML, Applied Materials) versus chip designers (Nvidia, Broadcom) in the AI boom. While equipment makers have outperformed over the past year, chip designers have higher profit margins (75-77% vs 50-54%) and greater pricing power, giving them a long-term advantage in capitalizing on the AI cycle despite massive capex investments expected to exceed $1 trillion next year.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong financial performance with 21% revenue growth and 28% earnings growth; near monopoly on EUV lithography systems; 150% share price increase over past year; positioned to benefit from continued AI investments and $1 trillion capex wave.

Solid financial results with 11% revenue growth and 20% earnings growth; essential provider of HBM memory and transistor equipment; 200% share price increase over past year; backbone of AI chip manufacturing.

Exceptional financial performance with 85% revenue growth and 140% earnings growth; dominant 86% data center GPU market share; industry-leading 75% gross margins providing pricing power and resilience; clear winner over 3-year period; best positioned for long-term AI cycle advantage.

Strong growth with 48% revenue increase and 54% earnings growth; leading custom ASIC provider for major tech companies; high 77% gross margins enabling pricing power; 3-year performance winner; well-positioned to weather potential AI spending slowdowns.

title: Forget Taiwan Semiconductor: 2 AI Semiconductor Equipment Stocks to Buy and Hold Instead
author: Will Healy
description: The article argues that semiconductor equipment makers ASML and Applied Materials are better investment choices than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing due to geopolitical risks in Taiwan. ASML, the sole producer of EUV lithography machines, has seen 17% annual revenue growth and a 145% stock increase over the past year. Applied Materials, which provides equipment for various chip manufacturing processes, projects 18% revenue growth this year and 29% in 2027, with a 200% stock increase over the past year.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: ASML holds a monopoly on EUV lithography machines essential for advanced chip production. The company demonstrates strong financial performance with 17% annual revenue growth, 22% net income increase, and 145% stock appreciation over the past year. Its geographic location in the Netherlands mitigates geopolitical risks compared to Taiwan-based competitors.

Applied Materials benefits from high AI chip demand with projected accelerating growth of 18% this year and 29% in 2027. The stock has appreciated over 200% in the past year. While facing more competition than ASML, the company's diversified equipment portfolio positions it well for continued semiconductor industry expansion.

TSMC faces significant geopolitical risk due to its Taiwan-based manufacturing facilities. The article highlights that while invasion is unlikely, investors must account for the possibility of losing most production capacity, making it a riskier investment compared to equipment suppliers with safer geographic locations.

title: Got $100? 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory ETF to Buy Right Now.
author: Manali Pradhan, Cfa
description: The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) offers diversified exposure to the AI memory supply chain, including memory producers, chip designers, and equipment suppliers. Growing demand for high-bandwidth memory in AI accelerators is creating supply shortages expected to persist beyond 2027. While the recent semiconductor sell-off has improved entry points, the ETF trades at a premium valuation (66x earnings) with concentrated holdings, presenting downside risks if AI spending slows or memory supply increases faster than expected.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Positioned to benefit from sustained HBM demand and memory supply constraints through 2027; offers diversified exposure across the AI memory ecosystem; recent sell-off improved valuation entry point.

title: QQQ vs. VGT: Where Should You Invest $1,000 Right Now?
author: David Dierking
description: The article compares two tech-focused ETFs: Invesco QQQ (tracking Nasdaq-100) and Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT). QQQ offers better diversification with ~30% non-tech holdings providing downside protection, while VGT is a pure tech play with lower expenses (0.09% vs 0.10%). The author recommends QQQ for its balance amid inflation concerns and geopolitical risks, though both ETFs remain viable for those bullish on AI-driven earnings growth.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better choice due to sector diversification (30% non-tech), exposure to semiconductor leaders (Micron, Lam Research, Applied Materials), and downside protection against tech-focused market tumbles amid inflation and geopolitical concerns.

Positioned as a pure tech play suitable for those confident in AI rally continuation and double-digit earnings growth. Advantages include lower expense ratio (0.09%) and concentrated exposure to tech sector gains.
